title: Convert HTML to Next.js Components: index.html
description: This project aims to convert a standalone 'index.html' file into a functional Next.js application using TypeScript and the App Router pattern. It involves parsing HTML, extracting CSS and JavaScript, creating reusable React components, and integrating them into a Next.js project structure, ensuring responsiveness and maintainability.

tasks.title: Initialize Next.js Project Structure
tasks.description: Ensure a Next.js project exists. If not, create a new Next.js project with TypeScript and App Router. This task sets up the foundational directory structure required for the conversion, preparing the environment for subsequent steps. (Create todo list: 'Setup Next.js project' -> Input to task: `npx create-next-app@latest nextjs-project --typescript --app` -> Execute code: run command -> Review results: verify project structure).

tasks.title: Analyze Source HTML and Extract Head Content
tasks.description: Read the 'index.html' file to understand its overall structure, identify the main body content, and extract all elements within the <head> tag (meta tags, title, link rel, etc.). This step involves parsing the HTML to gather necessary information for migration and integrating head content into `app/layout.tsx`. (Create todo list: 'Parse HTML, extract head' -> Input to task: 'index.html content' -> Execute code: parser script/manual extraction -> Review results: verify `layout.tsx` for correct meta/title).

file_operations.description: Source HTML file to analyze and extract content from.
Integrate meta tags, title, and other head elements into the root layout. Error consideration: ensure correct JSX syntax for self-closing tags and attributes like `charset`.

tasks.title: Migrate Static Assets to Public Directory
tasks.description: Identify all static assets referenced in the HTML (images, fonts, favicons, etc.) and copy them to the `public` directory of the Next.js project. Update their paths in the original HTML/JSX during later conversion steps. (Create todo list: 'Move assets' -> Input to task: asset paths from HTML -> Execute code: copy command/script -> Review results: check `public` directory contents).

file_operations.description: Read HTML to identify static asset references (e.g., `` src, `link` href for favicons/fonts).
Read all identified static asset files from the input directory (assuming they are co-located). Error consideration: handle missing asset files gracefully.

tasks.title: Extract and Convert CSS to Next.js Styles
tasks.description: Extract all CSS from the original 'index.html' (inline styles, <style> tags, and linked .css files). Implement a strategy for styling in Next.js, prioritizing CSS Modules for component-specific styles and `globals.css` for global styles/resets. Convert CSS properties to their JSX equivalents if used directly in style attributes. (Create todo list: 'Extract styles, categorize' -> Input to task: HTML style content -> Execute code: extraction script/manual move -> Review results: check `globals.css` and temporary CSS module).

file_operations.description: Read HTML to extract inline styles, <style> blocks, and linked CSS file references.
Read any external CSS files linked in the HTML.
Add global CSS rules (e.g., resets, common utilities) extracted from the HTML. Error consideration: avoid CSS conflicts by carefully categorizing styles.
Create a temporary CSS Module file to hold styles that will later be distributed to individual components. This acts as an intermediate holding place.

tasks.title: Convert HTML Body to Initial Next.js Page Component
tasks.description: Take the main <body> content from 'index.html' and convert it into a basic JSX structure within `app/page.tsx`. This initial conversion will likely result in a single, large component. Ensure proper JSX syntax (e.g., `className` instead of `class`, self-closing tags, `htmlFor`). Update static asset paths to reference the `public` directory. (Create todo list: 'Convert body to JSX' -> Input to task: body HTML -> Execute code: conversion script/manual JSX conversion -> Review results: `page.tsx` created, check basic rendering with `npm run dev`).

file_operations.description: Read the <body> content of the source HTML.

Create the main page component containing the converted JSX from the HTML body. Asset paths (e.g., `src="/images/my-image.png"`) will be updated during this conversion. Error consideration: ensure all HTML attributes are converted to their React equivalents to prevent runtime errors.

tasks.title: Identify and Outline Reusable Components
tasks.description: Analyze the newly created `app/page.tsx` for logical sections (e.g., header, navigation, hero section, content blocks, footer) that can be refactored into smaller, reusable Next.js components. Create an outline of these potential components, including their suggested names and the JSX/CSS they would contain. (Create todo list: 'Component breakdown' -> Input to task: `page.tsx` content -> Execute code: manual identification/documentation -> Review results: outline document created, makes sense).

file_operations.description: Read the initial page component to identify componentization opportunities based on semantic structure and repeated patterns.
Read the temporary CSS module to understand styles that need to be coupled with new components.
Document outlining proposed components, their responsibilities, and style allocations. This helps plan the next task.

tasks.title: Develop and Integrate Individual Components
tasks.description: Based on the component outline, iteratively create individual `.tsx` component files (e.g., `Header.tsx`, `Footer.tsx`) within the `components/` directory. Move corresponding JSX and component-specific styles (creating `.module.css` files) into these new components. Replace the original large JSX blocks in `app/page.tsx` with instances of these new components. (Create todo list: 'Build component X' -> Input to task: JSX/CSS for component X -> Execute code: create files, move code -> Review results: `page.tsx` imports component, component renders correctly).

Create corresponding CSS module files for each new component.
Update the main page to import and use the new components, replacing their original HTML content.
Remove the temporary CSS module once all styles are distributed to individual component modules.

tasks.title: Integrate JavaScript Functionality
tasks.description: Analyze any JavaScript found in the original 'index.html' (<script> tags, inline event handlers). Convert imperative DOM manipulation into declarative React state management and `useEffect` hooks. For external scripts, consider using `next/script` or converting them to React components if applicable. (Create todo list: 'Migrate JS for feature X' -> Input to task: JS code block -> Execute code: refactor to React/Next.js -> Review results: feature X works as expected).

file_operations.description: Read HTML to identify JavaScript code in <script> tags or inline event handlers (`onclick`, `onload`).
Integrate page-level JavaScript logic using React hooks (e.g., `useState`, `useEffect`) or Next.js-specific features.
Integrate component-specific JavaScript logic using React hooks. Error consideration: ensure proper cleanup for `useEffect` hooks to prevent memory leaks.
Create a utility file for common JavaScript functions if extracted from the HTML.

tasks.title: Review, Refine, and Optimize Components
tasks.description: Perform a comprehensive review of all created Next.js components and the main page. Check for: correct JSX syntax, proper styling, responsive design, accessibility (ARIA attributes), SEO (meta tags, semantic HTML), and Next.js best practices (e.g., Image component for optimization, Link component for navigation). Refine code for readability and maintainability. Address any identified errors or warnings. (Create todo list: 'Review component Y for issues' -> Input to task: component Y code, visual check -> Execute code: refactor code -> Review results: component Y is clean and optimized).

file_operations.description: Review the main page component for best practices and correctness.
Review the layout component for correct head content and structure.
Review all individual components for correctness, styling, best practices, and potential performance optimizations.
Review component-specific CSS for proper application, consistency, and potential for simplification.
Apply refinements and optimizations to the main page, such as using `next/image` and `next/link`.
Apply refinements to the layout, if necessary (e.g., dynamic metadata).
Apply refinements and optimizations to individual components (e.g., prop typing, memoization).
Apply refinements to CSS modules, ensuring styles are scoped and efficient.

tasks.title: Test and Verify Converted Next.js Application
tasks.description: Run the Next.js development server (`npm run dev`) and thoroughly test the converted application. Verify all features, navigation, responsiveness, and visual elements against the original 'index.html'. Check the browser console for any errors or warnings. Ensure all static assets load correctly and JavaScript functionality works as expected. (Create todo list: 'Test responsiveness' -> Input to task: open browser -> Execute code: interact with app -> Review results: app functions, no errors).

file_operations.description: Start the Next.js development server to run the application locally.
Monitor for client-side errors, warnings, network requests, and performance metrics.
Compare the rendered Next.js application visually against the original HTML file to ensure fidelity.
Verify all generated and modified files for functionality in a live environment. This is an implicit read via the running application.

goals: Convert index.html to a Next.js application using TypeScript and the App Router.
Break down the HTML structure into modular, reusable React components.
Properly migrate and integrate CSS styles, preferably utilizing CSS Modules for component encapsulation and `globals.css` for overall application styles.
Integrate JavaScript functionality from the original HTML into declarative React patterns or `next/script`.
Ensure all static assets (images, fonts, favicons) are correctly handled and displayed by Next.js.
Produce a functional, maintainable, performant, and well-structured Next.js project that adheres to modern web development best practices.
